plain: To stir up, as trouble or a fight

webster.text: To incite; to set on; to provoke; to urge; used chiefly or wholly in an ill sense; as, to instigate one to evil; to instigate to a crime.

example.quote: The reader will easily perceive, that the doctor not only exerts his utmost abilities to instigate the deluded colonists to persevere in their rebellious courses, but labours to inflame their minds against the determinations of the British parliament.
example.cite: John Witherspoon, The Dominion of Providence over the Passions of Men (sermon, Princeton, May 17, 1776; 2nd ed. 1777)
